the reaction between the complex cyanide acids and the base is a proton transfer reaction, and that the proton transfer is facilitated by the presence of the complex anion.

the infrared spectra of solid, anhydrous complex cyanide acids show a single absorption in the region of 2,100–2,200 cm−1 which is assigned to the cyanide stretching frequency, and no absorption in the region 3,000–3,800 cm−1 which could be attributed either to the hydrogen stretching frequency or the hydrogen bending frequency.
The structure of the anhydrous complex cyanide acids of the transition metals, M(CN) 2 (M = Co, Ni, Cu, Zn, Hg, Au, Pd, Pt) is linear with a C ≡ N bond length of 1.15–1.20 Å.
